about: Every message Aaron typed or dictated in this session on Terra (the PC), copied verbatim from its log on 25 September 2026. Only his words. Taken from both places the log keeps them - the queued record of every message he sends and the plain user records - each message kept once at its earliest time. Messages he sent while Claude was still working sit in time order with the rest and are not marked apart, because a queued record alone does not show that. System text, tool output, skill instructions, task notifications, cross-session messages, compaction summaries and anything the studio wrote are excluded, as are the helper agents' logs beside this one. WARNING: this session's working folder was this project's, but its subject is the Resume Engine project, not the game. It is saved here because these are his words and this is the only log folder that holds them.
title: Resume-engine Phase 4 remediation

messages.text:
I'm continuing work on resume-engine, a project at C:\Users\aaron\resume-engine
that generates tailored resumes from a YAML corpus (corpus/master-resume.yaml)
by matching a job posting to tags, filtering/composing bullets, and rendering
to PDF/DOCX. Read CLAUDE.md at the project root first — it has the full rules.

STATUS: Phases 0-3 of a pre-beta remediation plan are complete and verified.
Phase 4 remains.

===== WHAT'S DONE =====

PHASE 2 — scripts/verify.py hardening (H1, H5, H2, M1)
- H1: verb escalation. _claimed_verbs() scans ALL verbs a bullet claims (not
  just the leading word), using VERB_RANK (60+ verbs, ranked 1-6) and
  ESCALATION_FORMS (inflected forms). _NOT_THE_SUBJECT and _ATTRIBUTED_AWAY
  regexes stop false positives on possessives ("the director's established
  direction") and passive attribution ("directed by Ryan Allsop").
- H5: ownership ceiling — REDESIGNED mid-implementation. Originally compared
  verb rank directly against the corpus `ownership` rung (1-6 scale); this
  rejected 24 of 121 real corpus bullets against their OWN text, because rung
  and verb strength are different scales (approved wording routinely pairs a
  strong verb with a low rung, e.g. "Directed the work of a junior
  videographer" is rung 2). Fixed: the ceiling is now RELATIVE, matching
  CLAUDE.md's actual rule — a composed bullet may not claim more than the
  SOURCE WORDING states. The rung is only a fallback ceiling when no source
  verb is recognizable at all.
- H2: proper nouns. Removed the "skip sentence-initial word" bug and the
  all-caps-<=4-chars exemption, so fabricated names/acronyms can't slip
  through at the start of a sentence or by being short.
- M1: cross-role citations. verify_bullet() takes an allowed_ids set; a
  bullet citing a source from a different role is rejected. apply.py builds
  a real role->bullet-id map since ids aren't prefix-derivable.
- Verified: 121/121 corpus bullets self-consistent, 968/968 realistic
  two-bullet merges pass (0% false-positive rate), 24 targeted probe tests
  pass, all 11 saved applications byte-identical to the pre-change baseline.

PHASE 3 — priority-aware composition
- New scripts/priority.py: one Claude call ranks the posting's ALREADY-
  MATCHED tags (from matching.py) into P1 (core ask) / P2 (explicitly
  required or recurring) / P3 (secondary). It can only rank tags it's given —
  anything it invents is dropped before compose.py ever sees it. Gated
  behind use_claude; falls back gracefully (composition proceeds without a
  hierarchy) if the API is unavailable.
- scripts/selection.py: each role now carries TWO bullet lists. `bullets`
  stays capped at MAX_BULLETS_PER_ROLE (unchanged — this is what renders
  when Claude isn't used, so that path is byte-identical to before).
  `_matched_bullets` is new: the FULL domain-gated, tag-matched pool,
  uncapped, read only by compose.py so Claude can see everything relevant
  and do its own trimming.
- scripts/compose.py: rewritten system prompt teaches Claude to use the
  priority tiers (P1/P2 stay granular and lead each role; P3 compresses into
  one bullet per role; never blend tiers in one line). Per-bullet payload now
  includes priority, ownership rung, and alt_framings (pre-approved alternate
  phrasings). MAX_TOKENS raised to 16000; a truncated response now raises a
  clear error instead of failing to parse. Request JSON is compact.
- scripts/apply.py: runs priority.prioritize() before composition, threads
  the tier map through, builds verify.py's fact-check ground truth from the
  FULL matched pool (not just the capped set), and mechanically truncates any
  role that still exceeds the cap after verification (plain code, not
  another model call). Both the priority result and composition report are
  written into selection.json.
- scripts/serve.py: added a "Priority hierarchy" panel to the results page,
  between "What was kept" and "Claude composition" — shows the inferred
  position signal and P1/P2/P3 tag chips (dark teal / medium blue / light
  gray). Verified rendering in-browser on a live test run.
- BUG FOUND AND FIXED during live verification: compose.py's prompt tells
  Claude alt_framings are "as trustworthy as the bullet's own text," but
  verify.py's ground-truth `sources` dict was built from `text` only — so a
  number and an award name that existed ONLY in an alt_framing got wrongly
  rejected as fabricated. Fixed by folding alt_framings into the same
  ground-truth string in apply.py. Re-verified: both previously-rejected
  bullets now pass; full regression suite (121/121, 968/968) re-run clean
  with the fix in place.
- Live end-to-end proof: real Claude call on the vivint posting produced
  zero hallucinated tags in the priority ranking, and composition returned
  <=6 bullets for every role on its own (the mechanical post-cap trim never
  had to fire) even though aaf.dir-ed alone had 15 bullets available.

===== OUTSTANDING: PHASE 4 =====
- M4: scripts/serve.py's _ACTIVE_DOMAINS is mutable module-level state shared
  across concurrent requests — a race condition under concurrent use. Fix by
  making it immutable (copy-on-read or pre-computed).
- L2: scripts/apply.py's main() hardcodes use_claude=False for the CLI path.
  Add a flag (e.g. --with-claude) so the CLI can opt into composition too.
- A from-scratch full-pipeline integration test with composition enabled on
  a real saved posting, purely as a final pre-beta smoke test (the live
  tests so far used throwaway folders that were cleaned up afterward).

===== DESIGN DECISIONS TO PRESERVE (don't relitigate these) =====
- Verb escalation is checked RELATIVE to source wording, never against the
  ownership rung directly — the rung is a fallback only.
- alt_framings are first-class sources: anything in them must be included
  wherever a bullet's ground truth is built for verification, not just its
  main `text`.
- The priority pass may only rank tags matching.py already found — it can
  never expand what a posting is considered to be about. This is what makes
  it safe to fail open (composition just proceeds without a hierarchy).
- Composition sees the FULL matched bullet pool per role, not the render
  cap. The cap is enforced only (a) for the no-Claude fallback render, and
  (b) as a mechanical post-verification backstop — never by pre-filtering
  what Claude gets to consider.
- Cross-role bullet merges are forbidden outright (CLAUDE.md rule), enforced
  in verify.py via the allowed_ids parameter.
- Corpus `ownership` rungs (54 of 121 bullets) were hand-assigned by the user
  after I proposed a table; treat them as ground truth, not something to
  second-guess or recompute.
